subject: math.SP
name: Quantum unique ergodicity on negatively curved surfaces
statement: For every connected compact smooth Riemannian surface of strictly negative curvature, must the microlocal measures of every sequence of L²-normalized Laplace eigenfunctions with eigenvalues tending to infinity converge to normalized Liouville measure on its unit cotangent bundle?
importance: It asks whether classical chaos eliminates all exceptional high-energy quantum concentration.
status_note: Quantum ergodicity gives a density-one subsequence. Arithmetic QUE theorems with Hecke eigenfunction hypotheses do not settle the general full-sequence question.

references.title: Nonnenmacher, Anatomy of quantum chaotic eigenstates

subject: math.SP
name: Bohigas–Giannoni–Schmit spectral statistics
statement: For the Dirichlet Laplacian on a Bunimovich stadium billiard, within a fixed reflection-symmetry sector and after unfolding by Weyl’s law, do high-energy local eigenvalue correlations converge to those of the Gaussian orthogonal ensemble?
importance: It is the central proposed link between classical chaotic dynamics and random-matrix spectral statistics.
status_note: The system is time-reversal invariant, hence the orthogonal ensemble is the predicted class. Numerical evidence is strong; no general rigorous derivation for this chaotic billiard is known.

references.title: Bohigas, Giannoni and Schmit, Characterization of chaotic quantum spectra and universality of level fluctuation laws

subject: math.SP
name: Berry’s local random-wave conjecture
statement: On a connected compact smooth negatively curved surface, does a density-one sequence of real Laplace eigenfunctions −Δφ=λφ, sampled at a uniformly random point and orthonormal frame in geodesic coordinates scaled by 1/√λ and normalized to unit variance, converge in local distribution to the isotropic monochromatic Gaussian field with covariance J₀(|x−y|)?
importance: It predicts the microscopic statistics of chaotic eigenfunctions, including nodal patterns and correlations.
status_note: Macroscopic quantum ergodicity and random-model calculations do not establish this Gaussian local limit for deterministic eigenfunctions.

references.title: Nonnenmacher, Anatomy of quantum chaotic eigenstates

subject: math.SP
name: Pólya’s eigenvalue conjecture for planar domains
statement: For every bounded Lipschitz planar domain Ω, do its ordered Dirichlet Laplace eigenvalues satisfy λ_k ≥ 4πk/area(Ω) for every k≥1?
importance: It predicts that the leading Weyl-law term already gives an exact bound at every spectral scale.
status_note: Tiling domains, disks and several other classes are proved. The assertion for arbitrary planar domains remains open.

references.title: Filonov, Levitin, Polterovich and Sher, Pólya’s conjecture for Euclidean balls

subject: math.SP
name: Ivrii’s billiard conjecture
statement: In every bounded Euclidean domain of dimension n≥2 with C∞ boundary, does the set of periodic billiard trajectories have Liouville measure zero in billiard phase space?
importance: It would establish the standard second term of Weyl’s eigenvalue asymptotics without an extra dynamical hypothesis.
status_note: Many geometries and periodic-orbit periods have been handled, but the universal smooth-domain assertion remains unproved.

subject: math.SP
name: Schiffer’s overdetermined eigenvalue conjecture
statement: If a bounded simply connected C∞ domain Ω⊂ℝ² admits a nonconstant solution Δu+λu=0 with λ>0, u constant on ∂Ω and ∂νu=0 on ∂Ω, must Ω be a disk?
importance: It links overdetermined spectral data to geometric rigidity and the Pompeiu problem.
status_note: The disk has such solutions. Results for special domain classes do not settle arbitrary smooth simply connected planar domains.

subject: math.SP
name: Weak-disorder Anderson delocalization on ℤ³
statement: For H_λ=−Δ+λV on ℓ²(ℤ³), with independent uniform[−1,1] site potentials, does every sufficiently small λ>0 produce almost surely a nonempty interval of absolutely continuous spectrum inside the free spectral band?
importance: It asks for a rigorous metallic phase in the standard three-dimensional random Schrödinger model.
status_note: Localization at strong disorder and near spectral edges is established. Delocalization results on trees or special random models do not settle the cubic lattice.

references.title: Aizenman and Warzel, Random Operators: Disorder Effects on Quantum Spectra and Dynamics

subject: math.SP
name: Sharp upper bound in Yau’s smooth nodal-set conjecture
statement: For every connected compact C∞ Riemannian n-manifold without boundary with n≥3, is there C depending only on the metric such that every nonzero Laplace eigenfunction −Δφ=λφ satisfies H^(n−1)({φ=0}) ≤ C√λ?
importance: It predicts the sharp geometric complexity of smooth-metric eigenfunctions at high energy.
status_note: The matching lower bound and the analytic-metric case are known; polynomial upper bounds for smooth metrics do not give the sharp square-root estimate.

references.title: Logunov, Nodal sets of Laplace eigenfunctions: proof of Nadirashvili’s conjecture and of the lower bound in Yau’s conjecture

subject: math.SP
name: Spectral determination of smooth convex planar drums
statement: If two bounded strictly convex planar domains with C∞ boundaries have identical Dirichlet Laplace spectra, must they be congruent?
importance: It asks whether the vibration frequencies determine the shape of a geometrically natural drum.
status_note: Noncongruent isospectral planar domains are known in broader classes. Local rigidity and symmetric or analytic special cases do not settle all smooth strictly convex domains.

references.title: Can one hear the shape of a drum?

subject: math.SP
name: Sharp three-dimensional Lieb–Thirring constant
statement: Determine the optimal constant L in Σ_j |E_j(−Δ+V)| ≤ L∫_{ℝ³} V_−(x)^(5/2)dx for real potentials with V_−∈L^(5/2)(ℝ³), where E_j are the negative eigenvalues counted with multiplicity.
importance: The sharp constant governs quantitative bounds on quantum bound states and kinetic energy.
status_note: Finiteness and bounds are established. This asks for the exact constant at exponent γ=1 in dimension three and does not assume a conjectured extremizer that may fail in other regimes.

references.title: Frank, The Lieb–Thirring inequalities: Recent results and open problems
